messages:
acme-ops: Hey team — our integration hit a bunch of 429s around 22:40 UTC. UI shows credits were topped up a minute before but API still returns 429s and our streaming session got cut. Any idea?

maria: Sorry about that — can you paste the org id and the time of the top-up txn? also which endpoint you were hitting (stream vs REST)?

acme-ops: org_acme-42, top-up txn id tx_2026_05_03_2240, we were on a long-running websocket stream to /v1/stream/generate and then started seeing immediate 429s mid-stream. UI shows +5000 credits, but the client saw 429s right after.

jess: I can see tx_2026_05_03_2240 processed at 2026-05-03T22:40:12Z, amount +5000 credits. Billing processed and entitlement updated at 22:40:15Z. No failed steps from invoice side.

ashok: Thx, looking at enforcement logs. We see the edge enforcer still applying old quota until it fetches the new entitlement from the control plane. In normal cases that happens within a few seconds — but I see one edge node for org_acme-42 reported an NTP jump (clock moved backwards by ~40s) at 22:40:10 which triggered a ttl cache revalidation mismatch.

leo: To add — long-lived streaming sessions are charged token accounting as they stream. Some enforcers keep a local synced token-bucket view and only reconcile periodically. If control plane and edge disagree briefly, the edge can return 429 even though entitlement changed. This is exacerbated when a node's clock jumps.

acme-ops: so why did the UI show credits and we still got 429s immediately?

maria: UI reads from control plane (fresh after top-up). The streaming edge answered requests from a stale local cache slice that hadn't reconciled. That explains the mismatch.

ashok: Repro notes for eng: 1) start long streaming session 2) exhaust credits quickly via a burst 3) trigger a manual top-up 4) cause edge node to have clock rollback (simulate NTP jump) 5) observe edge returns 429 until reconcilation.

leo: Short term workarounds for customer: 1) reconnect the websocket stream (edge will re-evaluate entitlement on new session) 2) call the REST credits endpoint to confirm entitlement and force server-side sync:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/orgs/org_acme-42/credits
```
That will hit control plane and can nudge edge sync.

maria: Also try a quick GET to a low-cost endpoint after top-up to force edge refresh (e.g., GET /v1/health).

acme-ops: reconnect worked, streams resumed. Any permanent fix?

leo: We'll add a short mitigation: if an edge sees a top-up event but local clock drift > 5s or inconsistent ledger state, it should fallback to control-plane verification (sync-on-hit) instead of denying. I'll open ENGINFRA ticket and patch.

runtime-bot: deploy queued to eng-infra/edge-sync-fallback, changelist CL-#4321, est rollback-safe deploy window 2026-05-04 03:00 UTC.

jess: Billing side also added a reconciliation job to push an immediate invalidate event after manual top-ups for affected orgs — should reduce the window to <5s in most cases.

maria: Great, I'll mark this as escalated and reply to the customer with repro steps + reconnect workaround. @leo @ashok please add the NTP-clock-jump test to the chaos suite.

acme-ops: thanks — reconnect + the curl check fixed it for now :thumbsup:

maria: Follow-ups: ENGINFRA-4321 (edge sync fallback) and BILLING-2170 (post-topup invalidate). I'll update thread when deployments land.
